name: Badge
summary: A short piece of text that qualifies the item next to it: a status, a count, a category.
description: A badge is a small, read-only label attached to something else: the status of an order (Shipped), the number of unread messages, a category tag. It is text with a tinted or filled background; its intent gives the tint a meaning (success, warning, error, info), its emphasis how loud it is. A badge is never interactive: a removable tag or a filter is a different component.

anatomy.description: Root: a pill with the fill or tint of the emphasis and intent. Carries emphasis, intent and size.
The text. It is what assistive technology reads, in the flow of the content the badge qualifies.

options.description: Tinted fill with a light border and colored text: the default, for most statuses and tags.
Strong fill with a contrasting label: counts and the one status that must stand out.

properties.name: Intent
properties.description: Meaning of the color. Every intent exists at every emphasis.

options.description: No status meaning: categories, counts, tags.
Something new or highlighted by the product (New, Beta).

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Height, inline padding and text size scale together.

options.description: Inline in dense text, table cells (20 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: One or two words, or a number, that say the status or the category in text.

states.description: The only state: a badge has no interaction.

notes: The label is centered in a fully rounded pill whose minimum height and inline padding come from the size.
A badge sits inline with the text or the item it qualifies, aligned on its middle; it never wraps.

name.text: A badge has no accessible name of its own: it is text (a span with the generic role, for which naming is prohibited), read in the flow of the content it qualifies. The label is that text.

guidelines.text: A badge is read-only text: it exposes no role, no name and no state of its own; its label is read in place, after or inside the item it qualifies. Place it where that reading order makes sense.
Render a span with no ARIA role and no aria-label: the generic role prohibits naming, and the text is the content.
The intent color never carries the meaning alone: the label says the status in words (Failed, Shipped), so a badge without its color still reads.

Label text contrasts at least 4.5:1 with the badge fill in every color mode, emphasis and intent, on the default and level 1 surfaces: subtle 5.45:1 or more (light, error) and 9.60:1 or more (dark); accent neutral 16.29:1 and 13.84:1, brand 5.74:1 and 13.04:1, success 5.50:1 and 8.00:1, warning 11.43:1 (both), info 4.91:1 and 8.78:1. Known exception, from the Figma library's error colors: the accent error fill, 4.46:1 in both modes, tracked as a known issue.
The badge border is decoration: the text identifies the badge, so the light border of the subtle emphasis needs no 3:1 contrast.

A badge that appears or changes to report the result of an action (a count that increments, a status that flips) is a status message: the surrounding product announces it with a live region; the badge itself does not.
Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate meaning.

references.title: ARIA in HTML: span element (role generic, naming prohibited)
Apple HIG: Toggles, best practices (checkboxes and switches)

guidelines: One or two words in sentence case, or a number: Shipped, Needs review, 12.
Say the status, not the color: Failed, never Red.
Use the same words for the same status everywhere in a product.

decisions.text: A badge has two emphases, subtle (default) and accent, and six intents, neutral (default), brand, success, warning, error and info; each pair reads the Figma library's mapped roles for that emphasis and family: fill global.bg.<emphasis>.<family>.default, border global.border.<emphasis>.<family>.default, text global.text.on-<emphasis>.<family>.
A badge is a fully rounded pill with a 0.6 px border, 20 px high with 6 px inline padding and 12 px medium text (small) or 24 px high with 8 px padding and 14 px text (medium, the default).
A badge is read-only text with no role of its own and no interaction; a removable tag or a filter chip is another component.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions emphasis-and-intent, pill-sizes, read-only-text). A span with a label; emphases subtle and accent, six intents, sizes small and medium; no interaction state. Label contrast on its fill, light / dark: subtle neutral 12.09 / 11.82, brand 7.34 / 13.04, success 7.18 / 12.31, warning 7.28 / 12.85, error 5.45 / 9.60, info 6.92 / 11.41; accent neutral 16.29 / 13.84, brand 5.74 / 13.04, success 5.50 / 8.00, warning 11.43 / 11.43, error 4.46 / 4.46, info 4.91 / 8.78.
